title: Selves form only at intermediate levels of information sharing between subunits

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Selves form only at intermediate levels of information sharing between subunits

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Cognitive light cones grow or shrink as an agent's organization changes, and the key is a balance of selective information sharing through "synapses" (any structures that gate signals based on the state of others): too little sharing fails to bind subunits into a new Self, and too much yields an undifferentiated soup without modules or layered abstraction.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › Conclusion and Future Outlook

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Too little sharing results in a failure to bind subunits into a new Self. Too much sharing results in a homogenous soup with insufficient differentiation of modules and abstraction of information across distinct layers.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition”, Frontiers in psychology (2019), doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2019.02688; section “Conclusion and Future Outlook”. Scope: Multicellular and multi-agent biological systems

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2019-boundary-20: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.41

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: An intermediate optimum in integration and differentiation is testable in models and selected biological datasets. Calling that optimum Self formation is conceptual, and existing empirical sweeps are too sparse for the stated generality.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across controlled communication strengths in multicellular or multi-agent networks, quantify integration, modular differentiation, and collective task performance and test for an interior optimum rather than monotonic improvement.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Formation of a Self lacks an independent outcome metric.

Few public datasets systematically sweep communication strength.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The non-cognitive core is a Goldilocks effect of information sharing on modularity, which a gap-junction sweep in BETSE can exhibit or fail to exhibit. That is an analysis on public code, limited to the model. Calling the successful window a Self does not add a separate measurement, and tissue dose-response data are not assembled. The model can partially test the balance and cannot establish it for organisms.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Sweep a coupling or synaptic-gating parameter from isolation to full sharing and measure modularity of the resulting patterns or activity. An intermediate window with differentiated modules, flanked by fragmentation and by a homogeneous soup, would support the balance; monotone improvement with more sharing would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The location of the intermediate window depends on how sharing is parameterized.

Empirical dose-response of coupling versus anatomical modules is not one dataset.

What counts as a new Self is still a labeling choice.
